classification.recommended_terminology: cofinal actual-skip criterion for rational Mersenne membership
standard_mechanisms: greedy decoding and uniqueness for a strictly superincreasing subset-sum code

discouraged_terminology: cofinal skip proof for one half
classification.attribution: Credit Kakeya for the classical subsum-set setting, Merkle--Hellman for the standard superincreasing greedy-decoding paradigm, Kovač--Tao for the strict-tail unique-coding statement for these Lambert weights, and Erdős for irrationality of the full sum. Attribute the exact rational/cofinal-actual-skip equivalence and its Lean formalization to the local development without asserting priority.
classification.mathematical_interest: The result is not a new greedy algorithm. Its interest is the exact bidirectional interface: rational membership forces an infinite complement by full-sum irrationality, while the source's fatal-state theorem makes cofinal actual omissions sufficient for membership.
classification.reusable_scope: Positive rational-weight achievement systems with strict-tail unique greedy coding, irrational total mass, rational finite subsums, and an independently proved infinite-omission convergence theorem.
classification.why_it_matters: It unifies every nonnegative rational target behind one producer obligation. Future #257 arguments can be compared at the level of cofinal canonical skips instead of proliferating target-specific remainder languages, while the theorem itself is not confused with solving any one target.

primary_sources.author: Soichi Kakeya

primary_sources.title: Hiding Information and Signatures in Trapdoor Knapsacks
primary_sources.exact_anchor: The superincreasing knapsack is the easy private code: subset sums have unique digit recovery by the greedy algorithm.
primary_sources.supports: Canonical algorithmic antecedent for greedy decoding of superincreasing subset sums.

primary_sources.title: On arithmetical properties of Lambert series
primary_sources.author: Paul Erdős
primary_sources.venue: Journal of the Indian Mathematical Society, new series 12 (1948), 63-66
primary_sources.exact_anchor: The paper proves irrationality of $\sum_{n\ge1}1/(t^n-1)$ for every integer $t\ge2$.
primary_sources.supports: The load-bearing irrationality of the full Mersenne sum used to rule out a finite skipped complement for a rational represented target.
primary_sources.does_not_support: Achievement-set membership or greedy skip criteria.

primary_sources.title: On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Remark 13 proves $\sum_{l>n}1/(t^l-1)<1/(t^n-1)$ and concludes that the fixed-base Lambert subsums are mutually distinct and form a Cantor set.
primary_sources.supports: The exact strict-tail and unique-coding background for the Mersenne weights.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The canonical greedy cofinal-skip equivalence for rational targets.

mechanism_comparison.unique_greedy_code: Strict tail dominance makes each support code unique and permits greedy digit recovery.
mechanism_comparison.forward_rational_obstruction: If a represented rational had only finitely many actual skips, the irrational full sum would equal that rational target plus a finite rational correction.
mechanism_comparison.reverse_membership_consumer: Cofinal actual skips exclude every absorbing fatal state; the source theorem then makes the greedy selected sums converge to the target.
mechanism_comparison.positivity_boundary: For negative targets, greedy may skip forever while membership is impossible; $q=-1$ is the sharp displayed countermodel.
mechanism_comparison.canonicality_boundary: The skips must be generated by the target's canonical greedy orbit, not chosen as an arbitrary infinite complement.
